newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Scott Corp rated buy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Scott Corp rated buy.

text.p: Adelaide broker Day Cutten has downgraded its 1996/97 earnings forecast for transport contractor Scott Corp Ltd but issued a buy recommendation focussing on the profit outlook for 1997/98 to June 30.

"We have downgraded our earnings forecasts from A$6.5 million to A$6 million (excluding abnormals) for the 1996/97 year with the benefits of the expanded Smorgon contract now not expected to flow through until 1997/98," analyst Nick Ross said in a report. Scott Corp reported a A$5.7 million net profit before abnormals in 1995/96, on total sales of A$244 million.

Ross said profitability in 1996/97 would also be hampered by recent cost rises in distillate prices, which given current competition could not be passed onto clients, and a continuing relatively flat trading environment.

However, the benefits of recent interest rate drops should flow through to the retail and building materials sector in 1997, hence the broker's earnings forecast of A$7.5 million in 1997/98 remained intact, he said.
"Focussing on the 1997/98 profit outlook, the stock is attractive at current prices," he said.
Scott Corp shares closed on Friday at A$2.21.

Ross said average valuation, taking into account the weighted average earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation and price earnings ratio multiple for Scott, Finemore Holdings Ltd and Toll Holdings Ltd indicated fair value at around A$2.58.

Ross said while the building materials sector continued to remain relatively flat in the second quarter of 1996/97, volumes rose in areas such as timber and cement from the first quarter, helped in part by improved weather conditions.
"Specifically Scott's full truck load (FTL) division experienced a pick-up in volumes in the December quarter in line with the rise in building activity," he said.
"Less than truck load (LTL) and warehousing operations reported a lift in activity reflecting in part retailers expectations of a slight lift in Christmas sales," he said.
"The express component of the LTL operation has improved profitability in recent months with management refocussing the business and moving away from carrying unprofitable freight," he said.

Ross forecast 1996/97 sales of A$290 million, rising to A$325 million in 1997/98, with earnings per share rising to 20.1 cents in 1996/97 from 19.1 cents in 1995/96, and further to 25.1 cents in 1997/98.
